why: A gh-aw lock file carries its own role check, so the rule never judges it step by step, and it has to know a lock by what the compiler writes. The pass side, not applicable because no step of a lock is judged, is a lock on new issues whose agent job needs the activation job, which needs a role-check job whose step env admits admins, maintainers and writers. The fail side pastes the gh-aw header and a roles comment above a plain workflow that runs a base action with every permission prompt skipped under write-all on new issues; the review showed those two comment lines silenced the rule. Whoever judges locks step by step fails the pass side; whoever trusts the header passes the fail side.
